summary: Describes the Terms of Reference of RIPE (Reseaux IP Europeens), the cooperation of European IP networks. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: The rules of a club for European networks that work together.

questions: how does ripe coordinate european networks
what is a regional internet registry
subtitle: Charter of the European IP networks coordination body

tldr.problem: IP networks were expanding across Europe, crossing national and international boundaries, and needed technical and administrative coordination.
tldr.mechanism: RIPE (Reseaux IP Europeens) was created as a coordinating body to serve as a forum for technical information exchange, to promote interconnection of European IP networks with each other and to other continents, and to establish agreement on common management practices.
tldr.outcome: RIPE became a key regional Internet organization, analogous to ARIN and APNIC, and operates to this day as the Regional Internet Registry for Europe, Middle East and North Africa.

today: RFC 1181 is Informational. RIPE evolved into the Regional Internet Registry (RIR) for Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia, and continues to coordinate IP resources and policy for the region.

sections.title: Recognizing the Need
sections.content:
As IP networks grew beyond local area networks and extended over national and international wide-area networks across Europe, the need became clear for a body to coordinate their operation and expansion.

RIPE (Reseaux IP Europeens, or IP Networks Europe) was created to fill this role. The RFC outlines RIPE's Terms of Reference, which describe its objectives, scope and relationship to the networks it serves.
sections.plainLanguage: Many companies and universities had networks. They needed to agree on how to connect them together.

sections.title: RIPE's Objectives and Role
sections.content:
RIPE serves several purposes. It acts as a forum for exchanging technical information and building expertise on IP networking. It promotes and coordinates interconnection of IP networks within Europe and to other continents. It establishes agreement on common network management practices and operational management of interconnected networks. It also serves as a focal point for other common activities of its participants related to IP networking.

Importantly, RIPE is not a network service provider itself. The networks remain under the authority of their respective organizations; RIPE coordinates but does not control.
sections.plainLanguage: RIPE is a meeting place where network operators talk about how to connect fairly and agree on rules everyone can follow.

sections.title: Participation and Operations
sections.content:
All parties operating wide-area IP networks in Europe are encouraged to participate. RIPE operates as a collaborative body where member networks retain their independence. All documents produced by RIPE are made publicly available, reflecting the open nature of the Internet.

The RFC states that RIPE's area of relevance is Europe, distinguishing it from other regional coordinating bodies elsewhere in the world.
sections.plainLanguage: Any European network can join. They keep their own independence but work together and share what they learn.
